_about: Horace in English, translator per title: John Conington (verse; Odes and Carmen Saeculare; Satires, Epistles and Art of Poetry), the 'Handy Literal Translations' prose Works (translator unnamed), Eugene and Roswell Field's Echoes from the Sabine Farm (free verse versions). Clean Gutenberg. Dryden's Horace on the Dryden shelf (lane C). Latin-facing Loebs of 1930 or earlier added 2026-10-02 as raw IA OCR (translator per row); the scan's printing was checked for a post-1930 revision notice where its title verso survives. Perseus TEI English (section "perseus", fetched by pipeline/fetch_perseus.py): translations published in or before 1930; the TEI markup is Perseus Digital Library's, CC BY-SA 4.0 (attribution + share-alike), recorded per file in the report. Added 2026-10-03, verse Odes as raw IA OCR: C. S. Mathews (1867), H. H. Pierce (1884) and W. H. Cudworth (privately printed, 1917).

horace-bennett-loeb-odes.rights_override: Title page read: Bennett's Loeb Odes and Epodes, Harvard/Heinemann; the date OCRs as '1912' (the translation was first published 1914). The half-title lists later series editors (L. A. Post, E. H. Warmington), so the scan is a later impression; it carries no revision notice and its bibliography ends in 1912. Bennett died in 1921. Taken as the 1914 text, US public domain.

_collation.horace-literal-works: PG 14020 names no translator. Collated against horace-smart-buckley-1869 (Smart's prose revised by Buckley): 107 of 200 sampled 8-word runs match, against 3 of 200 for the unrevised 1756 scan (ECCO OCR, long s). So PG 14020 is Smart's translation in a revised form, probably Buckley's or one close to it; the exact revision is not established. Both are kept until Adam rules (2026-10-02)
